rationale: C25 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both letters frame European refugees and escapees as people risking danger to reach freedom, invoke America’s humanitarian tradition of providing a haven to the oppressed, and culminate in an appeal for prompt congressional immigration legislation. C07 shares the humanitarian and favorable-legislative-action structure but concerns genocide ratification; C21 shares the European escape-from-Communism and freedom language but lacks the legislative machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It is fundamental that free America remain an asylum for a substantial number of those who continue to risk their lives to reach freedom.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: escapees who have braved death to escape from behind the Iron Curtain. These refugees and escapees searching desperately for freedom look to the free world for haven.
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive parallel framing of European escapees risking death for freedom and seeking a haven in the free world.

shared_material.child_excerpt: fully in the spirit of one of our country's proudest traditions--that of offering a haven to the persecuted and oppressed.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: In order to help resolve this current immigration and refugee problem in the tradition of our American policy
shared_material.explanation: Both justify refugee admission by invoking a traditional American humanitarian policy toward oppressed people.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I will, of course, again urge such legislation in the next session of the Congress.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I recommend...the enactment of emergency immigration legislation... I urge that the Congress give this recommendation its earliest consideration.
shared_material.explanation: The later letter reprises the earlier operative objective: urging Congress to enact special immigration legislation for European refugees and escapees.
